title: Will Google ads read your Gmail? The one sentence Google changed on October 16
description:
Google's Privacy Policy effective October 16, 2026 added an unless to the line that it does not show personalized ads based on your Drive, Gmail or Photos content: unless you choose to make that data available to other Google services that support personalized ads. With one everyday comparison (handing a loyalty card to the cashier), this video shows which button that choice is, what ads get and do not get after you press it, and where the switch sits in your account.
For anyone with Gmail who saw the "Google wants your Gmail and photos for ads" headlines and wants to know: is that me, should I turn it off, and what do I lose?

Wording as seen on 2026-10-24: current policy vs the archived October 1 version. Apps, age, regions, the four steps, what Disconnect keeps, and the Personalized Recommendations path follow Google Search Help. Settings are still rolling out, so go by your own account. No Google Account was signed in; only public pages are shown. The "my view" lines are my opinion, not Google's. The Verge report (via Android Authority) is used for the timeline only. Not legal advice.

Settings pages: Search Services Personalization https://www.google.com/search-personalization/ ; My Ad Center https://myadcenter.google.com/ ; Search Services History https://myactivity.google.com/search-services/settings

Would you let AI search remember your plans if it also uses the summaries to pick ads? Tell me in the comments.

chapters.open: Will Google ads read my Gmail?
chapters.table: Does an advertiser see my inbox?
chapters.steps-off: What do I lose if I turn it all off?
chapters.my-call-1: My call: keep one switch, connect nothing

4273.text: Side by side you see a second difference: on the left, ads use only your interests and activity;

cyck.text: On October 16, one new sentence entered Google's Privacy Policy.

hbzk.text: Days later The Verge reported it: Google had added an exception to one of its promises.

gfvq.text: You may ask: if I connect Gmail to Google's AI search, will ads read my mail?

s6xc.text: Search reads summaries, draws inferences, and may use them to pick ads; but it won't hand your mail to advertisers.

duti.text: And it covers only one kind of user: those who pressed Connect themselves.

cbjq.text: In eight minutes you'll see that sentence, both versions side by side;

34p5.text: find the switch, three levels deep in your account;

twpb.text: and know which one to turn off without losing AI search personalization.

v7fy.text: Where is the change? In the paragraph on personalized services and ads, the second of three ad rules.

ba73.text: The previous version, just fifteen days old, ends the sentence at Photos. Full stop.

rbpf.text: The new version drops the full stop and adds an unless:

zyjc.text: unless you choose to make data from these services available to other Google services that support personalized ads.

8mvy.text: on the right, one more basis is added: personalized content from Google services.

37kx.text: Same version, one more example: some of the data you let Search access may be used to personalize content, including ads.

qdy7.text: The new version also adds a whole paragraph on which services you may let in to access your data: it names Search and Gemini Apps;

4scp.text: they may access data from Google Photos, Gmail and Drive, under the accessing service's own rules.

keqw.text: Quick to find on the page: scroll to the ad section, and rule two is right there.

48qj.text: So that “you choose” after the unless: which action is it, exactly?

mwqx.text: “You choose” is a single button: Connect, in your Google Account's Search personalization settings.

5nfe.text: You may ask, why would anyone connect?

rz4b.text: Connected, ask AI Mode for a restaurant, it checks where you've booked; ask about the weekend, it may check what you bought in Gmail.

c586.text: What connects is Google Workspace, today Gmail and Google Calendar;

g8yq.text: Calendar is only for US English accounts; Gmail in Taiwan works.

hpnd.text: The other is Google Photos, not open in every region;

3fvn.text: Taiwan is on the supported-countries list; whether Photos connects in Taiwan, I'm not sure, so don't assume it does.

7mh2.text: You turn it on yourself: off by default, eighteen and up;

xv9t.text: Can you undo it later? Yes; but undoing leaves one thing behind, and you'll see it shortly.

34j6.text: You may think connecting Photos just works? Not quite: in Photos you first turn on Face Groups and pick which face is you;

8n9h.text: and turn on Estimate missing locations; without both, Search gets no personalization from your library.

entd.text: Like a loyalty card: you hand it to the cashier to get discounts and deals;

ip9z.text: from then on, what you bought can become your next coupon; don't swipe, and the store doesn't know what you bought.

zy9n.text: Connect is handing the card over.

ryuw.text: One difference: the card only records this one purchase;

x7ux.text: one press of Connect, and all Search services can access your Workspace and Google Photos, not just one email.

pnub.text: “All Search services” is more than the search box: AI Mode counts, and so does Ask Maps;

fqdv.text: Shopping, Flights, all the way to News: hand that card over, and every door opens at once.

yx79.text: So once connected, can an advertiser really see my email?

h9id.text: Remember: your mail isn't handed over. What Search gets once connected is summaries of your mail and photos;

3pu4.text: plus excerpts and inferences: brands you often buy, the restaurants you like;

dspx.text: The same summary can be used to pick ads; advertisers don't even get your name or email address.

mdcm.text: “Not directly based on your inbox”: the key word is directly:

j6mz.text: The layer in between is summaries and inferences: the store uses your purchase history to pick coupons; the brand never gets your receipt.

8jv9.text: The same summaries also train models, on summaries, excerpts and inferences, not the whole inbox;

chw8.text: Human review: a small subset goes to reviewers, with protections first, such as detaching it from your account;

dbt8.text: Mail you don't want seen? Don't connect; Google wrote that itself. And if you already have?

xsz7.text: You may wonder how a summary differs from the full email. Mail too short to summarize? The summary may be the whole thing.

ptg5.text: A few categories are never used, connected or not: race, religion, sexual orientation, health.

n6xb.text: That rule is in both versions, not a word changed.

f25v.text: The example is in both versions: search mountain bikes, and YouTube shows you sports-gear ads.

75f6.text: Remember that unless from the opening? What it adds is this way in: the mountain-bike example gets one more ingredient.

7j2v.text: What your ads use, you can see and turn off in My Ad Center; link in the description.

awvf.text: So, am I connected right now? Open your account and one look tells you.

s3gu.text: Open the Search Services Personalization page in your Google Account; link in the description.

can6.text: Here, Personalized Recommendations must be on; if it's off, you can't press Connect.

nmqp.text: Then scroll down to Additional Personal Intelligence and tap Connected Content Apps.

b8y5.text: Remember the opening, three levels deep? This is the page.

8rnf.text: Next to Google Workspace and Google Photos: still says Connect? Nothing handed over yet.

tew4.text: Already connected? Disconnect here too; and remember that undoing leaves one thing behind?

nu96.text: The help page shows these four steps like this; link in the description.

n427.text: Disconnecting doesn't delete your Search Services History;

x8qf.text: like a store taking back the card while the purchase records stay at the counter.

bqmd.text: They can still improve products and train models; to clear them, go to the Search history page and delete; link below.

bdg5.text: So just turn it all off?

6cbd.text: That switch is one level up: open your Google Account,

w4bq.text: tap Data & privacy, then Personalization settings;

rjdj.text: and turn off Personalized Recommendations for Search services.

usjx.text: Off, Search still uses your current location and language; saved places and stock watchlists all stay;

dchc.text: Nor does it turn off or delete your search history.

hgcg.text: Here's the cost: AI Mode's personalization, Personal Intelligence, needs this switch and your search history both on;

2hu2.text: Off, and AI Mode forgets your tastes.

jqm3.text: The other path: leave the switch on, connect no Connected Content Apps; AI Mode still learns from your searches, and never touches mail or photos.

zu39.text: History stays because Search Services History is a separate switch, on another page.

ns6r.text: Turning it off, you choose off only, or off and delete history; both options sit on the same page.

dvnq.text: These settings are still rolling out; your account may still show the old names, so follow yours.

rbea.text: My view: this isn't a sneaky rule change; it writes an existing switch into the policy.

7qte.text: The way I use it: to let AI Mode remember my tastes, I keep Personalized Recommendations on;

sxya.text: and connect no Connected Content Apps.

tm32.text: If I ever connect Gmail to ask about travel plans, I accept first that my ads will change with it.

7qs5.text: I'd guess most people in Taiwan never pressed it; so check that page first, no rush to turn off all personalization.

cndn.text: Remember the opening question, will ads read your mail? Connect is a button you press yourself, and the ads follow that press.

q4bm.text: Would you let AI search remember your plans, if it also uses the summaries to pick ads? Tell me in the comments.

tn9i.text: Subscribe: every video gives you one decision you can make as soon as it ends.
